[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where QQQ's tape looked like this, the median 5-session return was -0.48%. When you condition specifically on a +2 sigma VIX spike, the path gets uncomfortable but rarely un-holdable: the median adverse excursion is only -1.05%, and 96% of those historical episodes stayed within a 10% drawdown over the week. The single number to anchor on for your volatility-spike question is that vol-spike p10 forward return of -5.26%.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs because the current state is defined by a severe liquidity contraction and an energy shock layered over mild recent volatility. The most distinctive feature is the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) at -2.262, meaning volume has collapsed well below its norm. That pairs with a WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) of 19.24%, while the 20-session realised volatility (vol20) sits at a quiet 13.24% and the distance from the 52-week high (dist52) is only -3.63%. These features pull in late-summer 2026 broad ETF sessions and scattered 2025 dates where liquidity dried up alongside commodity moves. Macro context shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a Fed funds target change over 90 days of 0.25 bp. Equity market sentiment is split: the engine-computed score is 57.1 ("Greed"), but the CNN Business Fear & Greed cross-check reads 38.3 ("fear"), driven by extreme fear in stock price strength and breadth components. Framing the symbol right now, Yahoo Finance · QQQ headlines note "Nasdaq, S&P 500, Dow Futures Steady Ahead Of Fed Minutes This Week" and ask "Is the AI Bull Market About to Crash? This Risk Indicator Is Saying Yes." Crypto sentiment (alternative.me crypto Fear & Greed at 70, "Greed") and crypto headlines apply only to the separate tokenised wrapper market, not to QQQ's equity mood.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of -0.09% and a median of -0.48%, with a standard deviation of 2.45%. The distribution leans slightly positive (skew 0.33), but the bad tail is populated by specific names: Morgan Stanley (MS) on 2026-09-04 returned -5.12%, Procter & Gamble (PG) on 2026-09-02 returned -3.16%, and IWM on 2026-09-08 returned -2.98%. The closest analog, QQQ itself on 2026-09-08, returned -1.92%. In 56% of the 50 episodes the 5-session return finished below zero, and only 2% of the analogs fell below -5%. The conformal interval, scaled to hit an 80% coverage target, spans from -3.69% to 2.73%, a total width of 6.42%.

[tails]
A position can end near flat and still be un-holdable mid-week. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -1.35%, while the 10th percentile of adverse excursions reached -3.7%. The probability of breaching a 5% drawdown intra-horizon was 6%. No analog breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown. The reward-to-risk ratio based on favourable versus adverse excursions was 0.85, meaning the upside paths were historically slightly smaller than the downside wicks.

[stress]
You asked about a two-sigma volatility spike. The dedicated "vol-spike" scenario (+2 sigma VIX) used 50 analogs and produced a median 5-session return of -0.18%, which is actually 0.3 better than the baseline median of -0.48%. However, the p10 forward return was -5.26%, and the median max adverse excursion was -1.05%. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 4%, meaning it was held within a 10% drawdown 96% of the time. The caveat is critical: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value.

Other scenarios worsen the picture materially. The "covid-crash" scenario dragged the median to -3.3% (a delta of -2.82% vs baseline), with a p10 of -11.99% and a 50% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; its caveat notes central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, baking the rebound into the returns. The "tariff-shock-2025" scenario produced a median of -0.68% but a p10 of -11.8% and a 26.9% breach probability; its caveat warns that policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The "carry-unwind-2024" scenario had a benign median of -0.39% but an 8.3% breach probability; its caveat states the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not.

Scenarios like "regional-banks-2023", "liquidity-air-pocket", and "crypto-contagion" actually improved the median versus baseline. None of the 14 scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
For your specific question about a two-sigma volatility spike making the path un-holdable, three scenarios matter most. First, the "vol-spike" scenario directly answers the prompt: across 50 analogs, the median adverse excursion was only -1.05% and the 10% drawdown breach probability was 4%, showing the path is historically holdable despite the p10 terminal return of -5.26%. Second, the "carry-unwind-2024" scenario is relevant because it isolates gap risk arriving from outside the equity complex, producing an 8.3% breach probability across 36 analogs despite a near-flat median of -0.39%. Third, the "tariff-shock-2025" scenario matters as a stress bound: across 26 analogs, it generated a 26.9% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown, showing what happens when a discrete shock overwhelms the usual vol mean-reversion.

A concentration to distrust: 22 of the 50 analogs are from 2025 and 17 are from 2026, heavily crowding the retrieval into very recent regimes and limiting out-of-sample diversity. No scenario contradicts the idea that a vol spike produces negative tail risk, but the vol-spike scenario's median (-0.18%) is actually less negative than the baseline (-0.48%), contradicting any assumption that the spike guarantees a steep median decline.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The honestVerdict states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 50.1%. For path risk validation, at the stated 10% drawdown level, the realised breach rate out of sample was 2%, while the mean predicted breach rate from the analog excursion share was 3.4%. The calibration gap is 1.4 pp with a clustered standard error of 0.48 pp. The analog Brier MAE was 0.0196, beating the vol reflection benchmark (0.0241), the same-name calibration (0.024), and the pooled calibration (0.021). The paired Brier confidence intervals resolve these differences: the analog beat vol reflection, same-name calibration, and pooled calibration in 100% of bootstrap samples, with all 95% CIs strictly negative (not spanning zero).

The wrapper status is "measured". On the primary venue (Bitget official MCP, QQQ/USDT perpetual), the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 62.09% of the wrapper's realised hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is a "fair" tracker with a return correlation of 0.9426 and a tracking error of 43 bp/day. The basis band is -0.11% to 0.48%, and the spread is 0.13 bps. The caveat is that this is a perpetual carrying funding and idiosyncratic risk, not the underlying, and nothing here feeds the retrieval engine.

For the return layer during closed hours: across 6 distinct weekend blocks observed on Bitget, the median weekend block return was -0.0665%, the p10 was -1.1155%, and the standard deviation was 0.8798%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.5825%. Zero percent of those 6 weekends breached a 5% drawdown threshold. Pooled across 39 instruments (which share the same 6 weekends, so 233 blocks overstate independence), the median return was -0.02% and 1.3% breached a 5% drawdown. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut, and they are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
